ai.title: Include exported tokens up to context limit
ai.summary: System prompt file tree generation now includes exported tokens up to a 75k budget. `ProjectFileContext` schema updated from `exportedTokens` to `fileTokenScores` with recursive token-based truncation logic. Tree-sitter language configs for Ruby, Go, Java, C#, C++, PHP, and Rust commented out in `common/src/codemap/languages.ts`. `printFileTreeWithTokens` added to `common/src/util/file.ts` for token-aware tree rendering.

eli5.text: When the assistant builds its mental map of your project files, it now pays attention to how important each file is and only includes the most important ones up to a size limit, so the overview it gets fits within its attention span. This means the file list you might see in prompts is smarter, less critical files get trimmed out automatically. It also quietly removes some less-used programming languages from its automatic analysis, and makes the file tree easier to read with consistent spacing. This change is live today and affects anyone whose code is being processed by the assistant.

ai.title: Reduce file tree token budgets and switch indentation to spaces
ai.summary: System prompt token budgets for truncated files and project file trees were reduced from 100k/75k to 80k/60k. File tree rendering in `common/src/util/file.ts` switched from tab to space indentation to minimize token consumption. Debug logging for token counts was added to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, while verbose parsing logs and exported token file writes were removed or commented out in `common/src/codemap/parse.ts` and `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`. These changes optimize context window usage and reduce noise in CLI output.

eli5.text: The project's file list view is now shown with spaces instead of the usual indented tabs, which trims down how much text is sent to you when the system summarizes your codebase. The system also caps the amount of code it pulls into your prompt and quietly logs its own usage in the background, while cleaning up some extra debug chatter that used to print during code parsing. You won't see this output directly, but it helps keep responses shorter and less cluttered.

ai.title: Reduce file request counts when assistant is asking
ai.summary: Adjusts `countPerRequest`, `numNonObviousPrompts`, and `numKeyPrompts` in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` to lower values when `assistantPrompt` is active. This change prevents excessive file requests during assistant-initiated queries. The modification is internal to the backend logic.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant (or another automated system) a question, the system now fetches fewer related files upfront instead of gathering many at once. Previously, every follow-up file look-up grabbed four files, three alternate prompts, and three key prompts; now, only one of each is pulled when the request comes from the assistant side. You would notice this as smaller, quicker file requests behind the scenes when the assistant is the one asking for more information. The change is already live and only affects assistant-initiated actions.

ai.title: Ignore mock projects in gitignore
ai.summary: `.gitignore` now excludes `__mock-projects__`. This prevents mock project directories from being tracked in the repo. Scope is the root `.gitignore` only; no model, CLI, Web, Desktop, or docs changes. Entry is appended after `.manicode`, and the file remains without a trailing newline.

eli5.text: Temporary practice project folders that the system uses for testing are now automatically hidden from the shared project storage, so they won't accidentally get saved or mixed in with real work. Only the project maintainers building the software will notice this; regular users won't see any difference.

ai.title: Update npm-app README wording and steps
ai.summary: npm-app/README.md intro and usage steps revised. Manicode description shifts to generating better code. Steps clarify running from project directory and simplify file I/O wording. Scope limited to npm-app documentation.

eli5.text: The short guide that explains how to use the terminal-based coding helper was rewritten to be clearer. The section that describes what the tool does and the steps for running it now read more simply, and the wording was tightened so you know to start the tool from within your project folder. If you opened the guide today, you'd see the new, less wordy instructions instead of the older, longer ones. The change is live now and only affects the text of that one guide.

ai.title: Rust language support added to codemap parser
ai.summary: Rust language parsing enabled in codemap via tree-sitter-rust. The `tree-sitter-rust-tags.scm` query was rewritten to simplify identifier extraction, replacing complex definition/reference tags with flat `@identifier` and `@call.identifier` captures. A `DEBUG_PARSING` flag gates verbose logging and token export logic in `parse.ts`. New `start-nushell` npm scripts added for local testing.

eli5.text: The codemap parser can now read and understand Rust projects. If you use the tool on a Rust codebase, you will see it generate an index of the project's symbols and structure instead of skipping the files. The change is live today.

ai.title: Rust tree-sitter queries index implitem tags
ai.summary: Added `impl_item` query patterns to `tree-sitter-rust-tags.scm` to capture trait and type implementations. This enables the codemap to index Rust `impl` blocks as callable tags. The change applies to the shared core `common/src/codemap` subsystem. Specific patterns match `trait` and `type` identifiers, with `!trait` ensuring type-only implementations are also captured.

eli5.text: You can now find Rust implementations of traits and types when searching across your codebase. The codemap now tags Rust 'impl' blocks as callable entries, so looking up a Rust type will show where it gains behavior. This works for both trait implementations and plain type implementations, with the latter matched even when no trait is involved.

ai.title: Java codemap support enabled
ai.summary: Java parsing enabled in `common/src/codemap/languages.ts` by uncommenting `JavaLanguage` import and config. `tree-sitter-java-tags.scm` updated to standardize capture names (`@identifier`, `@call.identifier`) and fix tag definitions for classes, interfaces, methods, and references. Scope limited to `common/src/codemap` subsystem.

eli5.text: If you open a Java project, you will now see its classes, interfaces, methods, and references mapped out instead of getting an unsupported or blank result. The tool turns Java source files into the same kind of overview it already builds for Python and JavaScript by enabling the built-in Java parser and aligning how it labels each code element. This works today for any project under the codemap feature, with no extra steps required from you.

ai.title: Codemap adds C, C++, C, Java, Rust language support
ai.summary: Uncommented and registered tree-sitter parsers for C, C++, C#, Java, and Rust in common/src/codemap/languages.ts. Updated tree-sitter query files (.scm) to use unified @identifier captures instead of granular @name.definition.* patterns. Added tree-sitter-c to package.json dependencies alongside existing language grammars.

eli5.text: The code map tool that shows the structure of your project can now read files written in C, C++, C#, and Java, in addition to the languages it already understood. When you open a project folder containing these files, the tool will now list their classes, functions, and other building blocks instead of skipping them. The change is already live today.

ai.title: Codemap adds Ruby, Go, PHP support and drops Elisp, Elixir, Elm, OCaml
ai.summary: Codemap now parses Ruby, Go, and PHP by uncommenting their tree-sitter configs and queries in languages.ts, while removing support for Elisp, Elixir, Elm, and OCaml. C files now use the dedicated tree-sitter-c-tags.scm query instead of the C++ one. Go and PHP queries were simplified to use generic @identifier captures, dropping complex doc-string stripping and specific definition/reference types.

eli5.text: If you use the code visualization tool, it can now map out Ruby, Go, and PHP code in addition to other languages it already supported. At the same time, it stopped supporting Elisp, Elixir, Elm, and OCaml, so if you rely on any of those, they will no longer appear in the diagrams. For C code, the tool now uses a more accurate set of rules to understand the structure, making the maps slightly more precise.

ai.title: Codemap test-langs replace greet functions with Greeter types
ai.summary: Test fixtures in `common/src/codemap/test-langs/` replace flat `greet` functions with `Greeter`/`Greeting` interface, class, struct patterns. Covers `test.c`, `test.cpp`, `test.cs`, `test.go`, `test.java`, `test.js`, `test.php`, `test.py`, `test.rb`, `test.rs`; deletes `test.el`, `test.ex`, `test.ml`, `test.ql`. Detail: `test.js` adds `createGreeter`, async `greetAsync`, array `map` coverage; `test.c` adds `malloc`/`free` lifecycle.

eli5.text: If you write a computer program that prints a greeting, this change swaps the old way of doing that simple print command for a more structured approach using containers and templates across 15 different programming languages. Instead of a single function that just outputs "Hello, World", the example code now defines a named object to hold the greeting settings, which makes the example more representative of real-world coding. This is housekeeping inside the software's internal test examples, so you won't notice anything different if you aren't writing code, but programmers building tools or learning these languages will see a more consistent and realistic pattern.

entries.title: Use green instead of blue/magenta. Use no color and bold for assistant response

ai.title: CLI uses green and bold text for status and responses
ai.summary: The CLI `npm-app/src/cli.ts` now uses `chalk.green` for status messages like Undo/Redo and 'Thinking...', and `chalk.bold` for assistant response chunks. This replaces previous `blue` and `magenta` colors to standardize visual cues. The change affects the CLI's display logic for navigation history, exit messages, loading spinners, and streamed output.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant in the terminal, status messages like 'Undo last change', 'Thinking...', and the goodbye line now appear in green instead of the previous blue or magenta, and your assistant replies are shown in bold white text instead of blue. This is purely a visual styling change to how the text looks in the terminal window; no features or commands changed. If you use the terminal-based assistant, you will notice these color and font differences the next time it runs.

ai.title: Replace chalk with picocolors
ai.summary: Swaps `chalk` for `picocolors` in CLI and WebSocket client. Updates imports in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, `client.ts`, `index.ts`, `menu.ts`, and `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts`. Removes `chalk` dependency from `npm-app/package.json`, adds `picocolors`. Adjusts color function calls to use named exports (`green`, `yellow`, `bold`).

eli5.text: The assistant’s on-screen text, like the green prompt name, yellow warnings about new versions, and the colorful startup banner, now draws itself using a smaller text-coloring plugin instead of the old one. You wouldn’t literally see different colors; the same greens, yellows, and bold styles still appear. If you maintain or repackage this tool yourself, you’ll notice chalk is no longer listed as a project dependency that needs downloading and updating, and everything that previously used chalk now loads picocolors instead.

ai.title: Remove bold formatting from CLI stdout output
ai.summary: In `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, the `process.stdout.write` call inside `subscribeToResponse` now writes the raw `chunk` instead of `bold(chunk)`. This change removes the bold styling applied to streaming responses in the CLI. The modification is internal to the CLI package and affects how text is rendered to the standard output.

eli5.text: When you run the command-line tool, responses that stream in will now appear in plain text instead of bold text. This affects anyone using the CLI to interact with the assistant. If you looked at the terminal output, you would notice the text no longer appears in bold style. The change simply removes the formatting that was previously applied as each chunk of text arrived.

ai.title: Dynamic tree-sitter language loading
ai.summary: Refactors `common/src/codemap/languages.ts` to dynamically import `tree-sitter` language modules via `packageName` strings instead of static imports. Updates `parse.ts` and `project-files.ts` to handle async language config retrieval and token parsing. Improves startup performance by deferring native module loading.

eli5.text: When the app starts up, it now waits to load its language-parsing tools only when they are actually needed for a specific file type, instead of loading all of them at once during boot. You won't see a new menu or setting, but the initial launch should feel slightly faster because the heavy parsing modules load on demand. This affects the backend and codemap tooling that analyze project files, and it also lets new file types like Rust be parsed without changing the core loading logic.

ai.title: Swap chalk for picocolors in terminal tool handlers
ai.summary: npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts replaces `chalk` with `picocolors` for command output formatting. `chalk.blue` calls are swapped for `green` from `picocolors` in `handleRunTerminalCommand`. test/package.json adds `common` dependency; test/tsconfig.json removes `moduleResolution` and `skipLibCheck`.

eli5.text: The assistant now highlights command-line text it prints for you in green instead of blue, using a smaller, faster text-coloring library under the hood. If you run a terminal command through the assistant, the prompt and completion message will appear in green where they used to be blue; nothing else about how your command runs or what you see changes. This is a behind-the-scenes styling detail, not a new feature.
